title: Vue in an hour
summary: Build a small interactive component with Vue 3 and know how its reactivity works.

blocks.text: A Vue component is a `.vue` file with a template, a script and optional styles. It is one piece of the page that you can reuse.

items: Add a template with one button.
Import it in a parent and use it as a tag.

blocks.caption: A small counter
blocks.code:
<script setup lang="ts">
import { ref } from 'vue';

const count = ref(0);
</script>

<template>
  <button @click="count++">Clicked {{ count }} times</button>
</template>

blocks.label: What you already know from Laravel
blocks.text: A component is like a Blade component: a reusable piece of markup with its own data.

blocks.label: Say it like this in an interview
blocks.text: A component bundles markup, logic and style, so I can reuse one piece of UI in many places. See the [Vue docs](https://vuejs.org/guide/essentials/component-basics.html).

check.question: Name the three parts of a single-file component.
check.answer: The template, the script and the style.

deeper.text: Think of a component as a Lego brick. It has a shape, a colour and a way of clicking onto others.
Once you built the brick, you use it as often as you like without building it again.

blocks.text: A `ref` holds a value that Vue watches. When the value changes, the parts of the page that use it update by themselves.

blocks.label: What you already know from Laravel
blocks.text: It is a bit like an Eloquent attribute that tells the view when it changes.

blocks.label: Say it like this in an interview
blocks.text: A ref is a value that Vue tracks, so the page follows the data without manual DOM updates.

check.question: How do you read a ref inside the script?
check.answer: With `.value`. In the template Vue unwraps it for you.

deeper.text: A ref is like a whiteboard in a meeting room. Whoever looks at it sees the newest text.
When someone rewrites it, everyone who is looking sees the change at once.

exercise.title: Build a like button
exercise.intro: Make a button that counts likes and shows a message at ten.
steps: Show a message when the count reaches 10.

solution.text: Keep the count in a `ref` and test it with `v-if`.

quiz.question: Which part of a component holds the HTML?
How do you change a ref in the script?
What happens when a ref changes?
options: The parts that use it update
quiz.explanation: Vue updates what depends on the ref.
